title: Private Companies Provide Cash Advances to Their Employees as Exempt Moneylenders
what_it_is: Private Companies Provide Cash Advances to Their Employees as Exempt Moneylenders

sections.label: Moneylenders Act and excluded moneylenders
sections.summary: The Moneylenders Act 2008 prohibits moneylending without a licence, exemption or excluded status, and MinLaw does not regulate or track excluded moneylenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Moneylenders Act 2008, or MLA, prohibits persons from carrying on the business of moneylending unless they (a) are authorised to do so by licence, (b) have been granted an exemption, or (c) are excluded moneylenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: An “excluded moneylender” is a person falling within a list of definitions in the MLA and includes any person that lends solely to that person’s employees as an employment benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Law (MinLaw) does not regulate excluded moneylenders and does not maintain figures on the number of such moneylenders.

sections.label: Exempt moneylenders and GFin programme
sections.summary: Exempt moneylenders must observe borrowing cost restrictions, and GFin, a Grab subsidiary, intended to implement a Partner Cash Advance programme for Grab drivers and delivery partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In addition, exempt moneylenders, like licensed moneylenders, are required to observe borrowing cost restrictions, to prevent them from extending loans with exploitative interest rates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In this regard, GFin, a subsidiary of Grab, intended to implement its “Partner Cash Advance” programme for Grab drivers and delivery partners.

sections.label: GFin exemption granted by MinLaw
sections.summary: MinLaw granted GFin a three-year exemption in August 2022 after assessing its programme as safe and sustainable credit, and will apply the same framework to similar future applications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In granting the exemption to GFin, MinLaw assessed that its proposed programme provided an alternative source of safe and sustainable credit to their partners who might not qualify for other forms of credit or who may be charged high interest rates due to their irregular incomes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Having weighed these considerations, MinLaw granted GFin an exemption in August 2022 for a period of three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Should MinLaw receive other similar exemption applications in future, the same framework in which we assessed GFin’s application will be applied to these applications.
